hook_text: Two syringes, a straw, some cardboard and a basin of water. In two lessons it holds a block in its jaws.
clip_script: Write the order of work before you touch a knife: mark, cut, glue two layers, punch holes, build the block, fit the arms, pin the rod, fill with water, mount the syringe, test. Knife on a mat, along a steel ruler, light passes, cap it when you put it down. Glue two card strips with the ridges crossed and press them under a book: that is a stiff arm. Punch the holes, never cut them. Cross the arms on a split pin so pushing the back ends apart closes the jaws. Straw for the rod, pinned tight, no slack. Fill the syringes under water so there is not a bubble, then push gently. The jaws snap shut on a wooden block and hold it. Now measure everything against your brief, write met or not met, fix what failed and write that down too. That record is where the marks live.
visual_style: Whiteboard bench scene: numbered steps appearing down one side while a cardboard device assembles part by part and finally grips a block.
mood: Hands-on, calm and proud at the end.
pacing: Order of work as a rapid list, slower on the three craft tricks, then the satisfying grip and the test table.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your sequence of manufacture before the next making lesson.
